weightage.label: Literature Text Book and Supplementary Reading Text

note: Official CBSE theory paper: 80 marks. Reading Skills = 22, Creative Writing Skills = 18, Literature Text Book and Supplementary Reading Text = 40. Internal assessment is separate (Listening 5, Speaking 5 and Project Work 10) and is excluded from this private-candidate theory scope.
mistakes: Reading: answering from general knowledge instead of the passage; support answers with evidence from the given text.
Reading: confusing inference with a sentence copied from the passage; state the inference clearly and connect it to textual evidence.
Reading: overlooking the case-based visual/statistical input; use the information actually supplied in the passage and accompanying input.
Creative writing: losing marks through incorrect format, missing required parts, weak organisation, unsuitable tone, or ignoring the prescribed word range.
Creative writing: using memorised content that does not address the specific verbal/visual input.
Literature extracts: identifying an option or detail without explaining the relevant textual meaning when the question requires interpretation or inference.
Literature short answers: retelling the whole chapter instead of answering the exact inferential question in 40–50 words.
Literature: making character/theme claims without linking them to a relevant incident, image, event or textual reference.
Poetry: identifying a poetic feature without explaining its effect or connection to meaning when the question requires appreciation or analysis.
Vistas long answers: giving a chapter summary instead of demonstrating global comprehension and analytical/evaluative understanding.
Long answers: spending too much space on introduction and not developing the analytical or evaluative response within 120–150 words.
Internal assessment: spending this theory-tip section on Listening, Speaking or Project Work; those components are outside the private-candidate written-paper scope.
order: Finish Reading Skills first: practise both unseen-passage types and train specifically for comprehension, interpretation, analysis, inference, evaluation and vocabulary through inference.
Build separate format checklists for notice, formal/informal invitation and reply, job application with bio-data/resume, letter to the editor, article and report.
Practise all writing tasks within their prescribed word limits: up to 50 words for notice/invitation-reply and 120–150 words for letters, articles and reports.
Read all prescribed Flamingo prose and poetry actively, tracking central ideas, important incidents/images, themes and the textual evidence needed for inferential and analytical responses.
Read all prescribed Vistas texts for global comprehension, then practise incident/theme-based analytical and evaluative answers.
Practise extract questions separately for Flamingo poetry, Flamingo prose and Vistas prose because the assessed competencies differ slightly by source.
Practise 40–50-word literature short answers with direct, evidence-linked inference rather than chapter summaries.
Practise 120–150-word literature answers with analytical/evaluative development and relevant incidents, events, themes or extracts as reference points.
Finish with timed mixed-section papers using the current 22 + 18 + 40 theory structure, then review mistakes by comprehension, format, expression, evidence and interpretation.
Keep Listening, Speaking and Project Work separate from written-theory preparation.

resources.label: CBSE Class XII 2026-27 SQP & Marking Scheme

scope: CBSE Class XII English Core (301) 2026-27 written/theory Board-exam preparation; internal assessment (Listening, Speaking and Project Work) excluded for the private-candidate scope.

reference.label: Section A — Reading Skills
reference.text: Practise both prescribed unseen-passage types: one unseen passage that may be factual, descriptive or literary, and one unseen case-based factual passage using verbal/visual inputs such as statistical data or charts. The combined word limit for the two passages is 700–750 words. Focus on comprehension, interpretation, analysis, inference, evaluation and vocabulary through inference.

reference.label: Section B — Notice Writing
reference.text: Practise the prescribed notice-writing format and keep the response within the stated limit of up to 50 words. Make every required piece of information explicit and do not add irrelevant material.

reference.label: Section B — Formal/Informal Invitation and Reply
reference.text: Practise both formal and informal invitation/reply formats. Keep each response within 50 words and make sure the response type matches the prompt.

reference.label: Section B — Application for a Job with Bio-data/Resume
reference.text: Practise the prescribed job-application format using the given verbal/visual input. Keep the letter within 120–150 words and include the requested bio-data or resume component without adding unrelated information.

reference.label: Section B — Letter to the Editor
reference.text: Practise letters to the editor based on verbal/visual input and public-interest issues. The prescribed purpose is to give suggestions or opinion. Keep the response within 120–150 words and maintain the required formal structure.

reference.label: Section B — Article Writing
reference.text: Practise article writing in 120–150 words. Questions are based on verbal input and may be descriptive or analytical. Organise the response around the given subject rather than inserting memorised material.

reference.label: Section B — Report Writing
reference.text: Practise report writing in 120–150 words. Questions are based on verbal input and may be descriptive or analytical. Keep the report focused on the information supplied by the question.

reference.label: Section C — Literature question types
reference.text: Prepare for poetry extracts from Flamingo, prose extracts from Vistas and Flamingo, 40–50-word short answers, and 120–150-word long answers. Literature questions assess comprehension, interpretation, analysis, inference, evaluation, appreciation, critical thinking and extrapolation beyond/across the text. For long answers, use incidents, events, themes, passages or extracts from the prescribed texts as relevant reference points.

reference.label: Flamingo — The Last Lesson
reference.text: Revise the complete text for extract-based comprehension and interpretation, short inferential responses, and analytical/evaluative long-answer questions. Be able to connect relevant incidents and themes directly to the question.

reference.label: Flamingo — Lost Spring
reference.text: Revise the complete text for extract-based comprehension and interpretation, short inferential responses, and analytical/evaluative long-answer questions. Use relevant incidents and themes as evidence rather than retelling the whole text.

reference.label: Flamingo — Deep Water
reference.text: Revise the complete text for extract-based comprehension and interpretation, short inferential responses, and analytical/evaluative long-answer questions. Build answers from relevant incidents and the text's development rather than memorised summaries.

reference.label: Flamingo — The Rattrap
reference.text: Revise the complete text for extract-based comprehension and interpretation, short inferential responses, and analytical/evaluative long-answer questions. Support interpretations with relevant incidents, themes and events from the text.

reference.label: Flamingo — Indigo
reference.text: Revise the complete text for extract-based comprehension and interpretation, short inferential responses, and analytical/evaluative long-answer questions. Practise connecting the question to relevant incidents and themes.

reference.label: Flamingo — Poets and Pancakes
reference.text: Revise the complete text for prose extract questions, inferential short answers and analytical/evaluative long answers. Keep responses tied to relevant incidents, observations and themes from the prescribed text.

reference.label: Flamingo — The Interview
reference.text: Revise the complete text for prose extract questions, inferential short answers and analytical/evaluative long answers. Distinguish direct textual evidence from inference when answering.

reference.label: Flamingo — Going Places
reference.text: Revise the complete text for prose extract questions, inferential short answers and analytical/evaluative long answers. Answer the exact question using relevant incidents, events and themes.

reference.label: Flamingo Poetry — My Mother at Sixty-Six
reference.text: Prepare for a poetry extract with comprehension, interpretation, analysis, inference and appreciation. Revise the poem's central ideas, important images and relevant poetic features, and explain their connection to meaning when asked.

reference.label: Flamingo Poetry — Keeping Quiet
reference.text: Prepare for a poetry extract with comprehension, interpretation, analysis, inference and appreciation. Revise central ideas, important images and relevant poetic features, and connect them to the question.

reference.label: Flamingo Poetry — A Thing of Beauty
reference.text: Prepare for a poetry extract with comprehension, interpretation, analysis, inference and appreciation. Revise central ideas, important images and relevant poetic features, explaining their effect where required.

reference.label: Flamingo Poetry — A Roadside Stand
reference.text: Prepare for a poetry extract with comprehension, interpretation, analysis, inference and appreciation. Revise central ideas, important images and relevant poetic features, and support answers with textual reference.

reference.label: Flamingo Poetry — Aunt Jennifer's Tigers
reference.text: Prepare for a poetry extract with comprehension, interpretation, analysis, inference and appreciation. Revise central ideas, important images and relevant poetic features, and explain their connection to meaning.

reference.label: Vistas — The Third Level
reference.text: Prepare for prose extracts, 40–50-word inferential questions and 120–150-word analytical/evaluative questions. For long answers, use relevant incidents, events and themes and show global comprehension of the text.

reference.label: Vistas — The Tiger King
reference.text: Prepare for prose extracts, 40–50-word inferential questions and 120–150-word analytical/evaluative questions. Build answers from relevant incidents, events and themes rather than a memorised chapter summary.

reference.label: Vistas — Journey to the End of the Earth
reference.text: Prepare for prose extracts, 40–50-word inferential questions and 120–150-word analytical/evaluative questions. Demonstrate global comprehension and use relevant textual incidents, events and themes.

reference.label: Vistas — The Enemy
reference.text: Prepare for prose extracts, 40–50-word inferential questions and 120–150-word analytical/evaluative questions. Support interpretations with relevant incidents, events and themes from the text.

reference.label: Vistas — On the Face of It
reference.text: Prepare for prose extracts, 40–50-word inferential questions and 120–150-word analytical/evaluative questions. Keep responses tied to the prescribed text and use relevant incidents and themes.

reference.label: Vistas — Memories of Childhood
reference.text: Prepare both prescribed parts—The Cutting of My Long Hair and We Too are Human Beings—for prose-based questions. Practise inferential short answers and analytical/evaluative long answers using relevant incidents, events and themes.

certification_note: Tips were audited against the CBSE 2026-27 English Core (301) theory structure and prescribed literature/writing scope. Internal assessment is excluded for the private-candidate scope. The tips are study guidance, not official CBSE advice.
